", "signature": "", "type": "thinking"}, {"text": "Amazon RDS automated backups and manual snapshots are both point-in-time copies of your database, but they differ in how they're created, how long they're kept, and what they support.

## Automated Backups

- **Created automatically** by RDS once you enable them (enabled by default on instance creation).
- RDS takes a daily storage-volume snapshot during a configurable **backup window**, and **continuously captures transaction logs**.
- Because transaction logs are captured, automated backups support **point-in-time recovery (PITR)** — you can restore to any specific second within your retention period (typically up to the last 5 minutes).
- **Retention is time-bounded and configurable: 0 to 35 days.**
  - Setting the retention period to **0 disables** automated backups.
  - The default is **7 days** when the instance is created via the AWS Console, or **1 day** when created via the CLI/API.
- Backups older than the retention window are **automatically deleted**.
- By default they're **deleted when the DB instance is deleted**, though you can choose to retain them separately ("retained automated backups") until the retention period expires.

## Manual Snapshots

- **User-initiated** — you create them explicitly (console, CLI, or API), or they can be created by automation.
- They are **full snapshots only** (no continuous transaction logs), so a restore brings you back to the moment the snapshot was taken, not an arbitrary point in time.
- **Retention is indefinite** — a manual snapshot is kept **until you explicitly delete it**. There is no automatic expiration.
- They **persist even after the DB instance is deleted**.
- They can be **copied** across Regions and accounts and **shared** with other AWS accounts.

## Quick comparison

| Aspect | Automated backups | Manual snapshots |
|---|---|---|
| Who creates them | RDS, automatically | You (on demand) |
| Point-in-time recovery | Yes (transaction logs captured) | No (restore to snapshot time only) |
| Retention | 0–35 days (default 7 via console) | Indefinite, until you delete |
| Deleted with the instance | Yes (unless explicitly retained) | No — survive instance deletion |
| Cross-Region/account copy & share | Not directly | Yes |

**In short:** automated backups give you hands-off, time-limited protection with point-in-time recovery (up to 35 days), while manual snapshots are durable, long-term copies you control and keep for as long as you need.

{"type": "investigation_result", "text": "Amazon RDS automated backups and manual snapshots are both point-in-time copies of your database, but they differ in how they're created, how long they're kept, and what they support.

*Automated Backups*

• *Created automatically* by RDS once you enable them (enabled by default on instance creation).
• RDS takes a daily storage-volume snapshot during a configurable *backup window*, and *continuously captures transaction logs*.
• Because transaction logs are captured, automated backups support *point-in-time recovery (PITR)* — you can restore to any specific second within your retention period (typically up to the last 5 minutes).
• *Retention is time-bounded and configurable: 0 to 35 days.*
  • Setting the retention period to *0 disables* automated backups.
  • The default is *7 days* when the instance is created via the AWS Console, or *1 day* when created via the CLI/API.
• Backups older than the retention window are *automatically deleted*.
• By default they're *deleted when the DB instance is deleted*, though you can choose to retain them separately ("retained automated backups") until the retention period expires.

*Manual Snapshots*

• *User-initiated* — you create them explicitly (console, CLI, or API), or they can be created by automation.
• They are *full snapshots only* (no continuous transaction logs), so a restore brings you back to the moment the snapshot was taken, not an arbitrary point in time.
• *Retention is indefinite* — a manual snapshot is kept *until you explicitly delete it*. There is no automatic expiration.
• They *persist even after the DB instance is deleted*.
• They can be *copied* across Regions and accounts and *shared* with other AWS accounts.

*Quick comparison*

Aspect  Automated backups  Manual snapshots

Who creates them  RDS, automatically  You (on demand)
Point-in-time recovery  Yes (transaction logs captured)  No (restore to snapshot time only)
Retention  0–35 days (default 7 via console)  Indefinite, until you delete
Deleted with the instance  Yes (unless explicitly retained)  No — survive instance deletion
Cross-Region/account copy & share  Not directly  Yes

*In short:* automated backups give you hands-off, time-limited protection with point-in-time recovery (up to 35 days), while manual snapshots are durable, long-term copies you control and keep for as long as you need.
